title: inter
oneLiner: Unisex garments made for the equality of all people.

cover.alt: Catalogue spread: two people in lilac knitwear, white blouses and skirts or trousers lean back in a field under a grey sky; on the right page a close-up of their clasped hands in the field.

facts.Context: fashion course, 4th semester, University of Applied Sciences Würzburg
facts.Role: design, pattern making and sewing (50/50), styling, film, photography, editorial design of the course catalogue
facts.Tools: fashion design, upcycling, styling, film, photography, editorial design

sections.label: Between
text: Inter stands for "between two or more": for equality, unconditional togetherness and the basic pillar of resilience that these values form. Why should the shells we wear divide and categorize us? We want to break with clichés and roles. Men can wear skirts, too. Clothing is clothing, and we humans are the core.

media.alt: Catalogue spread: on the left the names Rebecca Burkhardt and Felicitas Ferch and the project text, on the right two people in white blouses and lilac knitwear holding each other, with the hand-drawn title inter.

sections.label: Garments
text: All garments are either reassembled from existing clothes or tailored from scratch. The looks combine flowing white blouses and skirts with lilac knitwear and sage-green suit pieces, photographed outdoors with both of us as models. We also filmed the project, and I edited the film. In addition we designed and produced the catalogue for the whole course, from layout to final print.
